findings.issue: Non-404 upstream errors (or fetch rejections) propagate through query/createAsync with no ErrorBoundary anywhere in the tree, so an API hiccup renders a crashed page instead of an error UI.
findings.suggestion: Add a route-level ErrorBoundary (or catch in the query layer and render a fallback section) so upstream failures degrade gracefully.

findings.issue: The input-sync effect only copies the URL's q into the text signal when no debounce timer is pending, so navigating Back within the 150ms debounce window leaves the input and the URL out of sync.
findings.suggestion: Sync from the URL unconditionally on q change and cancel any pending timer, or key the effect on a monotonic navigation source.

findings.issue: Roughly twenty `any` casts (types, abilities, moves, evolution nodes) bypass the otherwise well-defined types.ts contract, hiding shape errors at runtime.
findings.suggestion: Declare minimal request-shape interfaces in lib/types.ts (the API shape is stable and documented) and drop the casts.

findings.issue: Expired cache entries are only deleted every 500th write; a crawl of all ~1025 species pages can transiently retain a very large map of cached API bodies.
findings.suggestion: Sweep on a timer or on every write when the map exceeds a size cap, or cap entry count with a simple LRU.

findings.issue: SearchParam array handling is duplicated: a `first()` helper exists in routes/index.tsx:8 but an inline variant is re-implemented here for params.game.
findings.suggestion: Move `first()` into lib/format.ts (or a small router-utils module) and use it in both routes.

summary: A genuinely idiomatic SolidStart v2 app: current stable stack, documented query/preload/MetaProvider patterns, clean routes→queries→server-module layering and no server/client leakage. The main gaps a reviewer would flag are the total absence of error handling for upstream API failures, some `any` casts in the server module, and a small debounce/back-navigation race. I'd merge after one light round of fixes.
